title: ReplicatedFirst
summary: The container whose contents replicate before anything else. LocalScripts here run earliest on the client — ideal for loading screens and bootstrapping before the world streams in.

details.heading: Ordering guarantee
details.body: ReplicatedFirst contents are guaranteed to replicate to the client before other services' contents. LocalScripts inside run before most other client code.

details.heading: FinishLoading
details.body: Roblox normally proceeds automatically; the older manual 'FinishLoading' flow is deprecated — modern loading screens just build UI here and destroy it when game content is ready (e.g. wait for workspace content via ContentProvider or a signal).

explanation.whatItIs: The express lane: anything in this service is the first to reach the client, and LocalScripts here get a head start over everything else.
explanation.whyItExists: Loading screens must appear BEFORE the world does — otherwise players stare at nothing (or worse, see unpolished content stream in).
whenToUse: Client bootstrap code that must run before other systems
Early anti-cheat or integrity checks on the client (paired with server validation)
whenNotToUse: For ordinary shared content — ReplicatedStorage is the normal choice
Don't block forever waiting for 'everything' — design a graceful transition when the world is playable
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Client boot:
1. ReplicatedFirst arrives  ← your loading screen runs NOW
2. rest of the game streams in
3. destroy loading UI when ready
```
tips: Keep loading UI simple and self-contained (no dependencies on late-replicating objects)
Destroy the loading GUI once your 'ready' condition is met — don't leave it covering the screen
commonMistakes: Waiting for workspace content with brittle hard sleeps instead of readiness signals
Referencing ReplicatedStorage objects from ReplicatedFirst scripts without WaitForChild (they arrive later!)

examples.title: Minimal loading screen
examples.code:
-- ReplicatedFirst/Loading (LocalScript)
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local gui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
gui.IgnoreGuiInset = true
local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
label.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(20, 20, 25)
label.TextColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
label.Text = "Loading…"
label.Parent = gui
gui.Parent = playerGui

-- Wait for the world to be reasonably ready:
task.wait(3)   -- or a proper readiness check for your game
gui:Destroy()
print("Loading complete")
